candidates.change: B: mov [4A17h],bx (instr 3) -> mov [0B6E9h],bx; both mov cx,04A17h (startup b/d INT87 and zombie_entry b/d search) -> mov cx,0B6E9h, so all our own captures jump through the private cell [0B6E9h] (cell from B053; static scan finds no pool warrior containing E9 B6). A: push cs/pop es/mov ax,0F2E2h -> les ax,[si+zdata] (dw 0F2E2h,1000h appended at the end of A); mov ax,[4A17h]/mov [9769h],ax -> mov bp,[0B6E9h] (instr 4)/mov [9769h],bp (instr 5, as in rev0); INT87 replacement CX 0B6E9h; nop; mov [4A17h],bp at instr 9 = late write of our entry to the V6-family cell (steals their zom20a/b/d captures and any [4A17h] poisoner's); INT87 stays instr 10, phoenix_init stays turn 22; rest identical to rev0.

threatFindings.threat: A poisoner that knows the private cell 0B6E9h (adaptive counter)

recommendation: Do not promote D1. Screen ALL +0.0006 (no field gain), it is a working defense against [4A17h] poisoners (+0.14) and helps vs V4/V6 a little, but it lost to V6Guard in 3 of 3 threat jobs (-0.049 significant on 12 fresh cohorts). If someone picks this up: run ablations to find where the V6Guard loss comes from: (a) B-side private cell only (= B053 reloc), (b) D1 without the A les/layout change (steal after INT87 instead), (c) D1 with the steal at instr 5-6. Add the cell change to a combination only if the V6Guard loss disappears.
